name: The Shard Cities
seat: no single seat; the Glass Table rotates between member cities each season
summary: A league of three excavation city-states built into the mouths of buried Concord cities on the Glass Reach. Where the Well-League forbids digging, the Shard Cities' whole economy is digging: they mine the old world — glass, stonework, relics, and sometimes writing — and sell it north at ruinous markup.

government.title: Dig-Lords (one per city)
government.current: Dig-Lord Sarei of Vetchgate, Dig-Lord Ommu of the Third Mouth, Dig-Lord Ferrin of Saltglass
government.note: The Glass Table settles boundaries between digs; disputes are settled by which city's claim-stakes survive the season.

population.note: shoring engineers; the only ones the diggers trust underground

laws: City law is dig-law: claims, shares, and shoring-safety. The Edict of Silence is enforced at the docks (outbound papers searched) and nowhere else — what is found below stays below until sold.

relations.note: Water comes from League wells; relics flow north past League tolls.
Only the Roads will haul sealed crates without asking.
Outbound relic searches; inbound Censer buyers with deep purses.
Some Dig-Lords sell true texts to the Chain at 'misprint' prices.

history_notes: Founded by dig-camps that refused Well-League limits after the Salt Roads opened (~300 AA).
The Third Mouth's lower galleries were sealed 'by common consent' after the third disappearance — the consent of everyone except the Dig-Lord who funded the fourth expedition.
adventure_hooks: Players are hired to escort a sealed crate to Velkash — the crate hums, and the Roads' carriers refuse it.
A Dig-Lord offers players exclusive rights to a fresh gallery: first pick of finds, if they go down before the shorers.
A Censer buyer recognizes a sold text as genuine Song Unbinding page; players must trace it through three cities before the Nine do.
